strings.name: Ferdinand Marcos Jr.
strings.summary: The son of Ferdinand and Imelda Marcos, Marcos Jr. served in provincial government, Congress and the Senate. Returning after family exile, he won the presidency in 2022. His government addresses the economy and South China Sea security while critics challenge his portrayal of his father’s authoritarian rule. In 2026 he led ASEAN-chair diplomacy.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: His presidency influences economic, security and South China Sea policy, with enduring scrutiny of family politics and governance.
strings.facts.f1.label: Family background
strings.facts.f1.value: Son of former president Ferdinand Marcos and Imelda Marcos.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Oxford Special Diploma in Social Studies; attended Wharton without completing an MBA.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Administrative career
strings.highlights.h1.text: Moved from Ilocos Norte politics to Congress and the presidency.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Regional diplomacy
strings.highlights.h2.text: Participated in ASEAN and security cooperation as president.
strings.timeline.t1.title: ASEAN summit speech
strings.timeline.t1.text: Discussed regional economics, digital cooperation and external partners.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Becomes president
strings.timeline.t2.text: Sworn in following his election victory.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Vice-presidential defeat
strings.timeline.t3.text: Lost to Leni Robredo; his electoral challenge was dismissed in 2021.

strings.timeline.t5.title: Elected representative

strings.timeline.t6.text: First family member to return after the 1986 flight.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Vice governor
strings.timeline.t7.text: Became Ilocos Norte vice governor during his father’s rule.

strings.timeline.t8.text: Received a special diploma, distinct from an undergraduate degree.
